front.title: Verification Promotion Boundaries for Protocol Implementations

abstract.t:
Protocol implementations frequently combine specification checks, deterministic test vectors, security testing, independent reproduction, and release decisions. A common failure mode is evidence collapse: a result at one assurance level is silently treated as sufficient for a stronger conclusion.
This document defines Verification Promotion Boundaries (VPB), a machine-readable profile and state-transition procedure that separates specification validation, local conformance, independent reproduction, authorized security testing, and release eligibility. VPB also defines dual-state handling for specification defects: detecting a bad normative vector is negative evidence about the tested subject but may be positive fault-detection evidence about the verifier. Unknown evidence never promotes.
